plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, ensuring non-negative profit whenever you win. Shading the bid down only reduces the chance of winning profitable auctions without lowering the price paid. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds others' bids (profitable), and you pay only the second-highest bid, never more than your value. Shading the bid doesn't increase profit—it only risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot game with independent draws, there's no long-term learning needed; truthful bidding maximizes expected profit given my value of $20.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $20 maximizes my expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions; bidding higher risks winning at a loss. I will bid exactly my value.
